subject: Dedicated floor structure, warm-up credits, and phased ramp (TheraGen Labs)
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya@theragen.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael O'Neal <michael.oneal@theragen.com>, procurement@theragen.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discussion follow-up

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks for walking us through the options yesterday. A couple of clarifying questions from procurement before we get legal involved: can you outline a plan where we start with a smaller guaranteed floor for month 1–3 and then ramp into a larger committed pool? We have two concerns: 1) minimizing upfront spend during validation, and 2) ensuring SLOs during peak runs for model evaluation.

Also, any ability to provide warm-up credits (for model cache priming and PKI onboarding) would help justify a faster activation.

Looking for a short bullets response that I can forward internally.

— Priya
Senior Cloud Architect, TheraGen Labs
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@theragen.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Michael O'Neal <michael.oneal@theragen.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discussion follow-up

Priya —

Appreciate the clear ask. Short bullets for procurement and engineering below; attaching an updated proposal and a warm-up credits worksheet.

Plan A — Phased floor (recommended for validation):
- Month 0–1 (onboarding): 8 guaranteed GPUs (reserved), soft burst to 16 for short windows
- Month 2–3 (validation): scale to 24 guaranteed GPUs; autoscale bursts to 32 under load
- Month 4+ (production): 48 guaranteed GPUs with policy-based routing to regional spare pools

Economic alignment:
- We can apply a 4-week warm-up credit (credits redeemable against consumed tokens/compute) to offset model priming costs. See warmup-credits-breakdown.xlsx.
- Pricing: ramped discount tiers tied to minimums — lower effective unit price once you commit to Month 4 baseline (48 GPUs).

Operational notes:
- KV/prefix caching warms quickly with the warm-up credits applied to background priming jobs; expect 20–30% latency improvement after cache warm-up window.
- SLA: 99.5% uptime on dedicated floor; critical-path requests routed to fallback models in other zones if capacity constrained.

Next steps: if that aligns, we’ll produce a redlineable term sheet and a DocuSign for the initial 3-month commitment.

Attachments: theragen-dedicated-proposal_v2.pdf, warmup-credits-breakdown.xlsx

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Michael O'Neal <michael.oneal@theragen.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya@theragen.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jul 2028 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discussion follow-up

Thanks Evelyn — this is exactly what procurement needs. Two quick asks: 1) can you codify the warm-up credit as a line item in the proposal (amount and expiry), and 2) provide an early-termination / pro-rata example if we decide to stop after month 3? They want a numeric scenario to model cashflow.

If you can send those in an updated appendix we’ll be ready to spin the legal thread.

— Michael
Head of Procurement, TheraGen Labs
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Michael O'Neal <michael.oneal@theragen.com>, Priya Shah <priya@theragen.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jul 2028 11:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discussion follow-up

Michael, Priya —

Adding the numeric examples you asked for (high level):
- Warm-up credit: $15,000 one-time credit applied against first 60 days of usage; expires 90 days from activation. (Line item in updated appendix A.)
- Pro-rata early termination: For month 1–3 commitments we calculate unused guaranteed GPU value based on remaining full-month guarantees. Example scenarios included: 1) Terminate after month 2 — pro-rata refund of 50% of months 2–3 guaranteed baseline, minus onboarding one-time fees; 2) Terminate during month 3 — refund calculated on remaining full months only.

I attached a short table in the appendix of the proposal (theragen-dedicated-proposal_v2.pdf) but we can surface the spreadsheet if procurement wants a modeled CSV.

Operational clarifications for engineering: we’ll reserve dedicated hosts for the guaranteed floor with an immediate warm-up priority queue to allow KV cache priming jobs to run in parallel to customer traffic. This preserves SLOs while limiting cost during validation.

— Rishi
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Shah <priya@theragen.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jul 2028 16:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discussion follow-up

Team —

This looks good. Procurement wants the warm-up credit clearly called out on page 2 of the PDF and the sample pro-rata scenarios tab exported into a simple CSV. I’ve looped legal — they asked for a short change to the SLA clause to explicitly include warm-up priming as an excluded activity from throttling rules during the first 30 days.

If you can deliver the two items (PDF page callout + CSV export) by EOD Monday we’ll move to DocuSign.

Thanks —
Priya
Senior Cloud Architect, TheraGen Labs
